description:
FILED s470 (Fable, 2026-09-05) while attributing the multideref.t LOST-2 after s470bk (#1058).

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL main ee9a658 AND the pre-BK tree d54b798 -- identical on both PCL trees, so PRE-EXISTING):

  my @y; eval { local $y[0][0] = 5; print "B-in: $y[0][0]\n" };
  print "after=", (defined $y[0][0] ? "def" : "undef"), " y0=", (defined $y[0] ? "viv" : "undef"), "\n";
  perl: B-in: 5 / after=undef y0=viv        PCL: B-in: (empty) / after=undef y0=undef

  my @w; eval { my $q = local $w[0][0]; }; print "w0=", (defined $w[0] ? "viv" : "undef");
  perl: viv                                  PCL: undef

The local-element macros (p-local-array-elem / p-local-hash-elem, the #508-#510 family) take the element of an UNDEF intermediate without vivifying it, and the localized store then goes to a detached place -- the same DETACHED-box class #1058 closed for the plain lvalue accessors (p-gethash-box / p-aref-box now vivify a writable place).

FIX SHAPE: route the local-element macros' container access through the same vivifying accessor (rule 11: ONE reading), then probe that the RT #130727 corner (`@{local $x[0][0]} = 1`) STILL vivifies+assigns -- it is an accepted divergence registered in cl/skip-registry.lisp (not-supported.md, `local` section), not a target.  Probe file: session scratch bk/rt2.pl (shapes A-D).  Companion: op/local.t, op/multideref.t --jobs 1 before/after.  Guard rows in Pl/t/local-elem-02.t if its wall time allows, else a new file.


=== s470br MEASUREMENT (2026-09-05): THE CAUSE IS THE EMITTER, NOT THE MACROS ===
The task says the local-element macros take the element of an undef
intermediate without vivifying it.  Measured on f728637 + this session's tree,
the emitter DROPS THE INNER SUBSCRIPT ALTOGETHER:

    my @y; local $y[0][0] = 5;   ->  (p-local-array-elem-init @y 0 5 â¦)
    my %h; local $h{a}{b} = 5;   ->  (p-local-hash-elem-init %h "a" 5 â¦)

so PCL localizes $y[0] / $h{a} and assigns 5 to THAT, then the body's read of
$y[0][0] is (p-aref (p-aref @y 0) 0) = a subscript of the number 5 = undef.
That is why the body printed nothing: not a detached box, a DIFFERENT ELEMENT.
It is also silently WRONG in the write direction (the outer element is
clobbered for the duration of the local).

So the fix is TWO parts, and the first is not the one the task names:
 (a) the `local` emitter must keep the whole chain â localize the INNERMOST
     element, with the intermediates vivified as containers (which is #1150's
     mechanism: perl vivifies $y[0] here, probed `y0=viv`);
 (b) only then does the macro question (a vivifying container access) arise.
Do #1150 FIRST: (a) needs exactly the container-vivification #1150 builds.
The RT #130727 corner (`@{local $x[0][0]} = 1`) stays an accepted divergence
in cl/skip-registry.lisp either way.


=== s473a MEASUREMENT (2026-09-07, Opus) â NOT ATTEMPTED, and why ===
Re-probed on s473a's tip (5461cf87), perl 5.40.3 as oracle
(scratch/s473a/probes/m4.pl, shapes A-F):

  A  my @x; @{$x[0][0]} = 1              perl ok def=1 x0=viv   PCL ok def=1 x0=viv
  B  my @y; local $y[0][0] = 5           perl B-in:5, y0=viv    PCL B-in:(empty), y0=undef
  C  my @z; @{local $z[0][0]} = 1        perl died def=0        PCL ok def=1
  D  my @w; my $q = local $w[0][0]       perl w0=viv            PCL w0=undef
  E  my %h; local $h{a}{b} = 5           perl E-in:5, a=viv     PCL DIES
  F  my @t; local $t[0][0][0] = 9        perl F-in:9            PCL F-in:(empty)

TWO THINGS THE TASK TEXT DID NOT SAY.

(1) The HASH twin does not merely read empty â it DIES, with an SBCL type
    error the program then reports as a perl exception:
      Value of pcl::h in (sb-impl::gethash3 k h nil) is 5, not a hash-table.
    which follows straight from the s470br diagnosis: the emitter drops the
    inner subscript, so 5 is stored in $h{a} and the body's $h{a}{b} is a
    gethash ON THE NUMBER 5.  It is caught by an enclosing eval, so it is a
    trappable wrong answer rather than a crash, but it is not "reads empty".

(2) The RT #130727 corner (C) is UNCHANGED by s473a's two `local` fixes â
    PCL still `ok def=1` where perl dies without vivifying, which is exactly
    the verdict registered in cl/skip-registry.lisp and
    docs/not-supported.md's `local` section.  Re-state that after any future
    fix here: it is an ACCEPTED divergence, not a target.

EMISSION CONFIRMED (pl2cl on the tip), the s470br reading exactly:
  local $h{a}{b} = 5   ->  (p-local-hash-elem-init %h "a" 5 â¦)
  local $y[0][0] = 5   ->  (p-local-array-elem-init @y 0 5 â¦)

WHY s473a DID NOT TAKE IT.  The brief's rule: a member that needs NEW
mechanism stops with its measurement.  This one does â the task's own s470br
addendum says part (a) needs #1150's container vivification FIRST, and #1150
is DESIGNED, NOT BUILT (DECIDED Â§s470bt: `expand-autoviv` is the walker, its
base case is free, but `p-gethash`/`p-aref` are FUNCTIONS so it cannot be
reached from them; the shape is two one-line macros plus a wrap in the two
element emitters when the container is itself an accessor).  Routing the
existing macros through the vivifying accessors â what this task's headline
still says â would NOT fix B/E/F, because the wrong element is chosen before
any accessor runs.  ORDER: #1150, then (a) the emitter keeps the chain, then
(b) the macro's container access.

=== BLOCKER LANDED (s473b, 2026-09-07) ===
The blocker named here, #1241 (= #1150, the read-path intermediate
vivification), SHIPPED at commit dde02df9 â the emitter now marks a
dereferenced container with `p-viv-container` / `p-viv-array-container` and the
runtime's chain walker expands it, so a nested element's intermediate levels
exist by the time `local` runs.  #1190 was NOT built in s473b (its member list
was full); it stays a filler in the same accessor area, with the design in the
body above.


=== s506 note (Fable, 2026-10-04; review probe of s501t, ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s506/review/min/l1.pl) ===
The bug does NOT need an undef intermediate: with `my %h = (r => { k => 1 })`, `{ local $h{r}{k} = "L"; print $h{r}{k} }` prints undef on main e5d72352 (perl: L); the array twins `local $a[1]{n} = ...` / `local $a[0][1] = ...` likewise.  Only the INITIALISED form is wrong: `local $h{r}{k}; $h{r}{k} = 5` reads 5 and restores correctly.
THE TIED TWIN (after #155 merges): because the OUTER element is what gets localised, `local $tied[1]{n} = "LN"` calls EXISTS on the tie class of @tied -- and dies "Can`t locate object method EXISTS" on a class that does not define it (perl never calls it: the local is on the plain inner hash).  Re-probe r506-nested2.pl rows 26/27 when this is fixed.  Sibling crash: #2598.
subject: SILENT WRONG (pre-existing): `local` on a NESTED element drops the INNER SUBSCRIPT -- `local $y[0][0] = 5` localizes $y[0] and stores 5 THERE (reads empty inside the scope, $y[0] never vivified), and the hash twin `local $h{a}{b} = 5` DIES on a gethash of 5; needs #1150 FIRST (s473a)
